title: Length-adaptive bucketing and padding elimination to improve micro-batch shaping
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Background: Our serving runtime currently applies coarse static batching which pads every micro-batch to the longest sequence in the batch. For workloads with high sequence-length variance (e.g., chat histories + short queries), this leads to wasted compute and higher per-token cost. Goal: implement a length-adaptive bucketing layer and on-the-fly padding elimination at the micro-batch level (micro-batch shaping) to reduce padded tokens while preserving latency SLOs and compatibility with KV cache and attention kernel selection. Scope: 1) Bucketing policy that forms micro-batches by length ranges with dynamic thresholds learned from recent request distribution. 2) Runtime hooks to trim padding for prefill and to avoid full-tensor allocations for decode when possible. 3) Integration with kernel selector to choose attention kernels optimized for the resulting length distributions, including fallback rules for heterogeneous micro-batches. 4) Telemetry and canary rollout with gated flags. Non-goals: changing model topology, persistent KV cache format, or user-visible API changes.
acceptance_criteria: Reducing average padded-token ratio by >=35% for top 10 customer workloads in test corpus
End-to-end 95th percentile latency does not regress more than 8% on production-like traffic for small-latency SLO customers
No correctness regressions in logits or streaming outputs (unit+integration tests pass)
Kernel selector chooses shorter-sequence-optimized kernels for >70% of shaped micro-batches where applicable
Feature gated and rollbackable; rollout plan documented and tested in staging
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Spike completed — sampled 72M requests from last 30 days. Found median seq_len=24, 95th=512, mean padded ratio 0.42 on mixed chat workloads.
2026-02-24: Prototype bucketing algorithm implemented (length-histogram quantiles -> dynamic thresholds). Microbench harness shows 28% padded-token reduction on synthetic traffic.
2026-03-02: Implemented in-memory micro-batch layout that carries per-item length metadata to avoid full-width padding during prefill tensor construction.
2026-03-05: Hooked kernel selector to accept estimated effective_seq_len from bucketing; added fallback path to previous behavior when kernel/memory mismatch detected.
2026-03-09: Integration tests green; ran canary load with 5% traffic on staging cluster: cost-per-token estimate improved by 22% and P95 latency increased 5% for decode-heavy workloads.
2026-03-12: Addressed a cache-coherency bug (race on KV cache compact) discovered during canary; mitigation landed and canary resumed. Preparing runtime-1.20 candidate branch for internal review.
benchmarks: Microbench (gpu-a100, batch=64 synthetic): padded-token reduction 34%, throughput +18% for mixed-length workload
Staging canary (5% production): cost-per-100k-tokens down 22%, P95 latency +5% on decode-heavy; prefill latency unchanged
Edge-case (many identical long sequences): no regression vs baseline; small overhead (~2%) due to bucketing decision cost
implementation_notes: Bucketing policy learned in 60s sliding window with exponential smoothing; default to conservative 3 buckets (short/medium/long) and allow up to 6 for high variance tenants
Micro-batch layout stores lengths + offsets and uses scatter/gather kernels to avoid allocating full [B, S] prefill tensors when possible
For decode path, use per-request attention mask compression and invoke specialized attention kernels that accept variable-length sequences when supported
Fallback: if effective GPU memory/wavefront alignment would be harmed or if KV cache growth would be too fragmented, fall back to the legacy fixed-padding path
Added metric 'bucketing.decisions.per_minute' and 'bucketing.padded_token_ratio' to monitor live impact
risks: Fragmentation of GPU work leading to lower absolute throughput if too many tiny buckets are created
Kernel coverage: some attention kernels don't support compressed masks and will force fallback; maintenance overhead grows with kernel matrix
Interaction with KV cache compaction can expose races (fixed in mitigation but needs further testing under bursty traffic),
Telemetry noise: early smoothing parameters may overfit recent spikes and produce unstable bucket boundaries
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start with internal tenants only (10% of internal traffic)
Gradually increase to 30% external canary, monitor padded_token_ratio, cost estimates, and P95 latency for SLO tenants
If metrics stable for 72 hours, expand to 60% with automated rollback thresholds (P95 latency +10% or error rate > baseline +0.25%)
Full rollout cleanup: remove feature gate after one release cycle and document config knobs in runtime-ops playbook
notes_for_reviewers: Key trade-offs to evaluate: how aggressive should the default bucket count be? We biased conservative to avoid fragmentation on shared clusters.
Please validate the kernel fallback heuristics — they are critical to avoid memory blowups on certain long-seq models.
Requesting review from infra-kernel team and SRE for canary thresholds and rollback rules.
